block: University workflows on the real local server (week 7)
reviewCheckpoint: 032e63986a170081cdaafbf897c84b60b8c08387 (founder, 29 Oct). This work comes after it.
kind: REAL SERVER, not fixtures. Compare docs/evidence/university-screens-local-2026-10-29.json, which is a fixture-harness check.
server: tools/browser-checks/accounts-local-server.mjs runs the worker's own handleAccountRequest, Better Auth and the real schema (schema.sql, organisations.sql) on in-memory SQLite behind the D1 interface. Every /api/ answer comes from the worker code; nothing is a fixture.
differencesFromCloudflare: SQLite through the same D1 shim the tests use, not D1 itself
The local server plays the TLS edge: the browser talks http to 127.0.0.1 and the worker sees https://localhost (Origin and Referer mapped the same way)
Sign-in codes go to a local outbox; no email is sent. A local-only /__dev/as helper signs the browser in as a fictional person
/orivia-nav.js is served from workers/trial-ui/nav.js (the trial worker serves an embedded copy)
No Workers AI, Browser Rendering, R2 or OpenAI; nothing reaches Cloudflare or any other service
people: Fictional only: owner, admin, student and outsider @northbay.example. Northbay University is fictional and set in Dubai.

walkthrough.how: By hand in the browser pane, through the screens: owner invites the partner admin; admin submits details; owner approves; admin checks welcome defaults, drafts and publishes a guide, creates a student invitation; student pastes the link and asks to join; student is refused before approval; admin approves; student sees the guide and sends a support request
walkthrough.note: The run ended when my local table helper crashed the server (a bug in the helper, not the worker). It was fixed, and the workflow was written as a replayable script so a restart can't lose it.

replay.tool: node tools/browser-checks/university-workflow-local.mjs (the same requests the screens send)

steps.step: Owner creates a named partner setup invitation
Another account cannot open that invitation
Invited admin opens it
Admin submits public details for review
Admin cannot approve their own application
Owner approves
Welcome defaults carried over from the application
Admin drafts a members-only guide
Admin publishes it
Admin creates a 7-day student invitation for 5 places
Student opens the invitation
Student asks to join
Before approval: no student space
Before approval: no staff content list
Admin approves the request
After approval: the student space shows the published guide
Student sends a support request (not forwardable)
Admin sees the request
Admin cannot forward it to Orivia without consent
Admin replies and marks it resolved
Student sees the reply
Application records stay locked for admins
A student cannot see the member list
An outsider cannot see the organisation
Progress totals stay paused below the reporting minimum
Activity history records the changes

ticket.title: Visa medical appointment
ticket.reply: Collect it from the Student Hub, Building A, with your passport.

ciTest: tests/university-workflow-real-server.test.mjs starts the server on a spare port and requires all 26 steps to pass

screenshots.set: owner overview and partner review; student space; 11 staff tabs, all at 390x844, after the replay
screenshots.result: No horizontal overflow and no error banners on any screen
screenshots.where: Shared privately with the reviewer, not committed

fixedFromThisCheck: Activity history showed raw action names ("invitation created", "content drafted") and called a staff approval "Joined". Every action the server writes now has a plain label
The owner's partner review listed raw keys (contactEmail: …, country: uae). It now shows field names and plain values
Support status options showed raw values (in_progress) in the university and Orivia inboxes. They now read Open / In progress / Resolved
(Earlier the same day, from the fixture check) workbench area, field and status names
notCovered: The app's own join entry (/?organisation=…#join=…) in the trial worker; the student used the /platform paste-a-link route
Students marking guides done (the Overview text mentions it; the /platform student space has no control for it)
AI guide drafting (needs OpenAI, which isn't connected locally)
Real D1, real email delivery, the Cloudflare edge
status: Visual review and language review remain pending. No guide review records were created. Nothing was deployed.

findingsFixedLater.when: 2026-10-29, after the founder asked for the seven findings to be fixed
fixed: Partner form: country, emirate/nation and reason are now dropdowns with the server's own values; the region list follows the country
Partner form: once submitted, it shows the details read-only, with "Change these details" (the server still accepts a correction while pending)
Member lists show the email once when an account has no separate name
Students are called "Student" in member lists and on the student's own home, matching the role control
The admin Support tab is an inbox ("Student support requests") without the members' send form; editors keep the member view
A staff reply writes a support.<status> activity entry in the same batch as the change; a stale reply is refused with 409 and records nothing
Data request types and statuses have plain names for students and in the owner's inbox
findingsFixedLater.alsoCorrected: My earlier partner-review label map used the wrong reason keys (family, other); it now uses the server's values (join or bring my family, something else)
findingsFixedLater.checkedOnRealServer: Browser on the real local server: partner form choices, region list, pending view and Change these details, as a second fictional partner (Eastgate College, Edinburgh); staff Support, Members and Activity, student home and owner review screenshots (5, shared privately)
findingsFixedLater.test: tests/university-workflow-real-server.test.mjs: 27 steps, and the activity history holds support.resolved exactly once
